cases.title: Bell-state preparation: the first entangled target
cases.semanticTier: exact finite matrix certificate + reviewed H/CX resource transcript
cases.problem: Starting from |00>, prepare the Bell state (|00>+|11>)/sqrt(2), so the case introduces entanglement rather than another one-qubit amplitude change.
cases.contract: Lean proves the target norm, a full 4 by 4 unitary completion, its exact zero-input column, and the two-gate resource tuple. The H-then-CX transcript is the familiar implementation view; the exact finite matrix certificate remains the proof authority.
symbols: controlled-X that correlates the second qubit with the first

cases.summary: The smallest state-preparation case where the target cannot be understood as two independent classical bit choices: coherence plus CX creates entanglement.

cases.title: Dense real-amplitude preparation: a Möttönen-style two-qubit benchmark
cases.semanticTier: exact two-qubit matrix certificate + paper-motivated UCRY resource transcript
cases.problem: Prepare the genuinely dense non-product real state with amplitudes (1,2,4,10)/11 and expose the binary-tree / uniformly-controlled-rotation structure used by general dense state preparation.
cases.contract: Lean proves that 1^2+2^2+4^2+10^2=11^2, verifies a rational quaternion unitary completion, proves its first column is exactly the target, and records the five-gate root-RY plus one-control-UCRY transcript.
symbols: a uniformly controlled y rotation: the target rotation angle depends coherently on control bits
split probability mass recursively before choosing amplitudes inside each branch
a normalized dense state chosen so the finite certificate is exact rather than floating point

stages.label: Conditional amplitudes

evolution.caption: The fixed benchmark uses the same recursive UCRY idea as dense arbitrary-state synthesis, while carefully stopping short of claiming the paper-wide n-qubit gate-count theorem is reproduced.

stages.name: Dense UCRY tree
stages.description: Exact target/unitary/state action are certified; the five-gate transcript is machine-counted at the repository resource tier.

qiskit.role: Numerically instantiates the two-qubit binary-tree angles for inspection; the exact Lean target certificate is independent of floating point.

cases.summary: A non-product dense state connects the textbook first-column contract to the uniformly-controlled-rotation architecture used for general state synthesis.
cases.source: Möttönen et al., Transformation of quantum states using uniformly controlled rotations, arXiv:quant-ph/0407010
cases.limitations: The fixed two-qubit state and resource transcript are formalized. The arbitrary-n state-to-state theorem, phase synthesis, and paper-wide complexity formulas remain in Papers/reproduction queue.

cases.title: Structured probability loading: product structure beats the generic tree
cases.semanticTier: exact structured two-qubit certificate + same-target resource comparison
cases.problem: Prepare amplitudes (9,12,12,16)/25, whose probabilities come from two identical Bernoulli factors. Compare a generic binary tree with a construction that exposes the product structure.
cases.contract: The same exact target and unitary certificate back both candidates. The generic tree is scored (5,5,0,0); exploiting the factorization gives two independent rotations in one layer, scored (2,1,0,0). Lean proves strict lexicographic improvement after correctness.
symbols: Grover–Rudolph's general setting uses efficiently computable probability mass splits
here the finite distribution factors into two identical one-bit distributions

stages.label: Use factorization
stages.detail: two identical independent RY rotations can run in parallel

evolution.caption: Both points use the same certified target. The second point is allowed to say strictly better because a named Lean betterThan theorem compares the frozen resource tuples.

stages.name: Factorized product route
stages.description: The product distribution removes conditional branching and exposes two parallel rotations.

qiskit.role: Replays both fixed two-qubit routes numerically. The resource dominance theorem is in Lean.

cases.summary: A structured probability-loading example demonstrates the core ASPBE point for state preparation: preserve the target while exploiting structure to make the certified resource tuple strictly smaller.
cases.source: Grover and Rudolph, Creating superpositions that correspond to efficiently integrable probability distributions, arXiv:quant-ph/0208112
cases.limitations: This exact factorized finite benchmark is not the general efficiently-integrable recursive theorem; integration/arithmetic oracle costs remain queued for reproduction.

cases.title: Sparse state preparation: prune the zero branches
cases.semanticTier: exact d=3 finite certificate + sparse-vs-dense transcript comparison
cases.problem: Prepare a three-qubit state with only d=3 nonzero amplitudes, (|000>+2|010>+2|100>)/3, and make the savings from zero branches visible before discussing asymptotic sparse-state algorithms.
cases.contract: Lean proves exact normalization, a full 8 by 8 unitary completion, and the first-column state action. A frozen dense three-qubit tree is scored (15,15,0,0), while pruning the identically-zero final branch yields (5,5,0,0); a named betterThan theorem certifies the strict comparison.
symbols: only d computational-basis amplitudes are nonzero
do not synthesize conditional rotations for subtrees whose amplitudes are known to vanish
a finite witness used to teach the mechanism, not the asymptotic theorem of the sparse-state paper

stages.label: Prune zero support

evolution.caption: The fixed d=3 example isolates why sparsity can help. The asymptotic circuit-size theorem is deliberately kept in the Papers queue until its actual construction and lower bounds are formalized.

stages.name: Sparse pruned tree

qiskit.role: Numerically demonstrates the fixed sparse target and pruned route; Lean owns the exact certificate and resource comparison.

cases.summary: A fixed sparse target shows the local mechanism behind sparse preparation: an exact certificate can remain unchanged while known-zero amplitude subtrees disappear from the resource transcript.
cases.source: Jingquan Luo and Lvzhou Li, Circuit Complexity of Sparse Quantum State Preparation, arXiv:2406.16142
cases.limitations: Only a fixed d=3 benchmark and a frozen transcript comparison are formalized; the paper's asymptotic constructions, ancilla tradeoffs, and lower bounds are not claimed reproduced.

bell-state-preparation.readerGoal: Understand why state preparation is about coherent amplitudes and phases, not just sampling a classical distribution.
bell-state-preparation.whyThisCase: The Bell state is the first example where the output cannot be described as two independently prepared qubits. A local superposition followed by an entangling CX makes the two wires share one joint quantum state.
bell-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Entangled resource states, teleportation, phase estimation subroutines, error correction, and many distributed protocols begin with small certified state preparations of this kind.
circuitReading: CX copies the computational-basis branch label coherently to q1, producing |00>+|11>.
The useful object is the coherent joint state before measurement.

theorems.label: Case theorem
theorems.title: The exact Bell target is prepared by a unitary completion
theorems.statementProse: Lean checks target normalization, full 4 by 4 unitarity, exact zero-input state action, and the two-gate resource record.
proofSteps: Use the Bell-basis unitary whose first column is the requested state.
The four Bell-basis columns are orthonormal.
Matrix-vector action on |00> selects exactly that first column.
Record H then CX as the reviewed two-gate transcript.

mottonen-dense-state-preparation.readerGoal: See how a dense target leads naturally to a hierarchy of probability splits and uniformly controlled rotations.
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.whyThisCase: A generic dense state has no obvious product or sparse shortcut. The finite two-qubit example makes the recursive Möttönen-style architecture visible without hiding the target behind floating-point amplitudes.
mottonen-dense-state-preparation.algorithmContext: General dense state initialization is an input-access cost for many amplitude-encoded algorithms. Möttönen et al. organize arbitrary state transformations with uniformly controlled rotations; this case certifies one exact real-amplitude specialization.

source.title: Transformation of quantum states using uniformly controlled rotations
source.authors: Mikko Möttönen, Juha J. Vartiainen, Ville Bergholm, Martti M. Salomaa
source.queryExplanation: The paper supplies the general UCRY architecture. ASPBE formalizes this exact two-qubit benchmark and resource transcript, not the complete arbitrary-n theorem.

circuitReading: Choose how much total probability belongs to the q1=0 and q1=1 halves.
A uniformly controlled RY chooses the q0 amplitude ratio separately inside each q1 branch.
The preparation must be one column of a full unitary, not an isolated normalized vector.
Five fixed transcript gates do not prove the paper-wide asymptotic count theorem.

theorems.label: Finite paper benchmark
theorems.title: The dense state (1,2,4,10)/11 has an exact preparation certificate
theorems.statementProse: The target, rational unitary completion, first-column equality, and fixed binary-tree resource tuple are all machine checked.
proofSteps: A rational quaternion completion supplies three orthogonal companion columns.
The zero input selects the requested dense amplitudes.
The resource transcript is root RY plus one-control UCRY.

grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.readerGoal: Learn when structure in a probability distribution should change the preparation circuit rather than merely change its angles.
grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.whyThisCase: The target factors into two identical one-bit distributions. A generic binary tree is correct but wastes conditional structure; two independent rotations prepare exactly the same target.
grover-rudolph-product-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Grover–Rudolph shows how efficiently computable probability masses can drive state preparation. The fixed product example isolates the structural principle and gives ASPBE a clean same-target optimization theorem.

source.title: Creating superpositions that correspond to efficiently integrable probability distributions
source.queryExplanation: The paper treats efficiently integrable distributions in general. This page certifies one exact factorized distribution and explicitly leaves the general integration/oracle construction in the Papers queue.

circuitReading: First solve the problem without exploiting factorization: root split plus conditional split.
The four amplitudes are products of the same pair 3/5 and 4/5.
Prepare each qubit independently with the same RY.
The two rotations touch different qubits, so the frozen schedule has depth one.
Both candidates inherit the same exact target/unitary certificate before betterThan is proved.

theorems.label: Correctness theorem
theorems.title: The product distribution has an exact state-preparation certificate
theorems.statementProse: Lean checks normalization, full-unitary completion, and exact first-column equality.
proofSteps: The four target amplitudes are 9,12,12,16 divided by 25.
The explicit 4 by 4 product rotation is unitary.
Its first column is the target.
Correctness is shared before resource comparison.

improvement.title: Exploit product structure instead of paying for a conditional tree
improvement.statementProse: At the frozen resource-transcript tier, the factorized route uses two parallel one-qubit rotations while the generic tree uses five sequential slots. The same exact target certificate backs both records.
proofSteps: Both candidates prepare the same exact four amplitudes.
Root RY plus a one-control UCRY gives five transcript gates.
The target is a tensor product of two identical one-qubit states.
The two RY gates share no wire and occupy one layer.
The Lean betterThan theorem closes already at 2<5 gates.

sparse-three-state-preparation.readerGoal: See sparsity as missing amplitude subtrees that a preparation circuit should avoid synthesizing.
sparse-three-state-preparation.whyThisCase: Only three of eight amplitudes are nonzero. Before studying asymptotic sparse-state constructions, the fixed benchmark shows concretely why a structure-blind dense tree performs unnecessary work.
sparse-three-state-preparation.algorithmContext: Sparse state preparation targets inputs where d is much smaller than 2^n. Modern work studies circuit-size and ancilla tradeoffs; ASPBE starts with an exact d=3 witness and keeps the asymptotic theorem separate.

source.title: Circuit Complexity of Sparse Quantum State Preparation
source.shortQuote: d-sparse if it has only d non-zero amplitudes
source.queryExplanation: The paper proves asymptotic sparse-state circuit results. This page certifies only a fixed three-qubit d=3 benchmark and a frozen transcript comparison.

circuitReading: A full three-level binary tree reserves a q0 splitting layer even though q0 is always zero on the support.
Delete that identically-zero subtree and retain only q2 root plus q1 conditional split.
The exact 8 by 8 unitary certificate is unchanged.
A 5-vs-15 finite comparison is not the paper's asymptotic optimality theorem.

theorems.label: Sparse finite theorem
theorems.title: The d=3 target has an exact three-qubit preparation certificate
theorems.statementProse: Lean checks target normalization, an explicit 8 by 8 orthogonal/unitary completion, and the zero-input column.
proofSteps: Three rational orthogonal columns span the rows 0,2,4.
The remaining rows receive computational-basis columns.
All 64 finite matrix entries close exactly.
The target support and amplitudes are exactly recovered.

improvement.title: Prune the zero amplitude layer
improvement.statementProse: The frozen dense tree contains three amplitude-splitting levels; the fixed support makes the q0 level identically unnecessary. Lean certifies the resource-tuple comparison after the shared exact state certificate.
proofSteps: The unpruned tree uses 15 RY/CX slots at this reference tier.
Only root plus one-control split remain, five slots.
Lean closes 5<15 in the repository betterThan order.
